verifies: the build-path change this experiment required — `--regdata-dir=` and `--tag=` on scripts/stack/run_undistort_groups.sh. CLAUDE.md: a build-path change lands with its own verification in the same commit.
what_the_flag_claims: one gNN.seq per group; absent, the group registers normally and WRITES its donor; present, the group is handed it and does not re-register, so its reference frame and every homography are the donor arm's.
the_bracket_is_the_verification_not_the_: a pinned build that quietly re-registered would still produce a stack, so 'it ran' proves nothing. What proves it is that the SAME knob moves the canvas without the flag and does not move it with the flag, at the same geometry the product is built at.

arm_UNPINNED.where: 12 consecutive aug06/set-01 frames through run_undistort_pipeline.sh, one knob (--subsky-lights), each arm saving its own registration
arm_UNPINNED.reading: the knob moves the reference and the delivered canvas

arm_PINNED.where: aug06/set-01 group 1, 100 frames — the PRODUCTION member geometry, not a pilot
arm_PINNED.donor: datasets/aug06/l1_work/regdata/set-01/g01.seq, written by the donor arm, reference index 8
arm_PINNED.builder_log: registration PINNED from .../g01.seq — this arm does not re-register (ref frame + every transform are the donor's)
arm_PINNED.reading: IDENTICAL canvas across the same knob that moved it unpinned

the_knob_still_acted: 69,225,418 of 69,225,420 pixels differ between the donor member and the pinned arm member — 100.00%. This matters as much as the canvas: a pin that worked by accidentally disabling the treatment would also show an identical canvas. The geometry is frozen and the photometry is not, which is exactly the intended separation.
verdict: VERIFIED. The flag makes a difference it did not make before, in the direction claimed, at production geometry — and the product records which donor it used (REGPIN) so a later reader need not trust a build log.
scope: aug06/set-01 group 1, Siril 1.4.4 flatpak, this rig. The remaining 12 members are built through the same code path and every one of them prints the same PINNED line; the per-group canvases are checked against their donors across all 13 before the arms are composed.
the_second_flag: `--tag=` is verified structurally rather than by measurement: the arm wrote to work/groups_set-0X_l1arm and work/groups_set-0X_l1ctrl while the canonical work/groups_set-0X was left untouched, which the control fingerprint re-check confirms against md5. Without it an arm build lands on the control's members and the resume guard then SKIPS every group, so the arm would look built and BE the control — a silent failure, which is why it is a required flag rather than a convenience.
